takeaway: Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetrical small joint arthritis of the hands, sparing the DIP joints, with narrowed joint space, osteopenia and marginal erosions on X-ray.

question.text: A 35-year-old woman has painful, stiff, swollen hands. Two years on, the MCP joints are swollen and tender; X-ray shows narrowed joint space, osteoporosis and marginal erosions. Diagnosis?
question.say: A thirty-five-year-old woman develops pain, swelling and stiffness of her hands. Two years on, the metacarpophalangeal joints are swollen and tender. X-rays show a narrowed joint space, osteoporosis, and marginal erosions. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: Pain and swelling at the MCP joints of both hands.
lines.say: This woman has swelling and tenderness at the metacarpophalangeal joints of both hands.

lines.text: On the X-ray, little monsters nibble the joint margins: marginal erosions.
lines.say: (laugh) On the X-ray, little monsters are nibbling the joint margins. These are marginal erosions.

lines.text: The bones are thin too: osteoporosis.
lines.say: The bones are thin too: osteoporosis, also called periarticular osteopenia.
And look at the little fingertip, happily spared. The distal interphalangeal joints are spared.

lines.text: Remember: symmetrical small joint arthritis sparing the DIP is rheumatoid arthritis.
lines.say: Remember: symmetrical arthritis of the small joints of the hands, sparing the distal joints, is rheumatoid arthritis.
